## Servers per internal system

| System | Server | License | Install route | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| git | `mcp-server-git` 2026.11.18; none of its 14 tools fetches, pulls, pushes or clones | MIT (the repository is moving to Apache-2.0) | `pip install mcp-server-git`, then `python -m mcp_server_git`; or build the image from `src/git` | https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers |
| Gitea | official `gitea-mcp` v1.13.0; `-ca-cert` adds an internal CA | MIT | release binaries, or the image `docker.gitea.com/gitea-mcp-server` | https://gitea.com/gitea/gitea-mcp |
| Forgejo | no official server; the community `forgejo-mcp` is the only one found | GPL-3.0 | image `git.b4mad.industries/agentic-forges/forgejo-mcp`; vet it first | https://github.com/goern/forgejo-mcp |
| GitLab Self-Managed | built in, generally available since 19.5, Free tier and up, at `https://<host>/api/v4/mcp`; an admin must turn it on | not applicable | HTTP needs no extra software; stdio needs the `mcp-remote` bridge. Auth: OAuth (`mcp` scope) or a fine-grained PAT | https://docs.gitlab.com/user/gitlab_duo/model_context_protocol/mcp_server/ |
| Outline | built in; a self-hosted instance serves `https://<your-domain>/mcp`, Streamable HTTP only | not applicable | nothing to install; OAuth or an API key | https://docs.getoutline.com/s/guide/doc/mcp-6j9jtENNKL |
| Jira and Confluence Data Center | `mcp-atlassian` 0.24.8, community, "Not an official Atlassian product"; Jira DC 8.14+, Confluence DC 6.0+, Personal Access Token | MIT | wheels (below), or the image `ghcr.io/sooperset/mcp-atlassian` | https://github.com/sooperset/mcp-atlassian |
| PostgreSQL | Google's MCP Toolbox for Databases (`googleapis/mcp-toolbox`) v1.18.0, run with `--prebuilt=postgres`; telemetry is opt-in | Apache-2.0 | one static binary, or the image `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/database-toolbox/toolbox/toolbox:$VERSION` | https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/releases/latest |
| Wiki.js, BookStack | no official server found; community servers exist and were not vetted | not documented | not documented | https://github.com/orgs/requarks/repositories?q=mcp |

- Atlassian's own server is cloud-hosted and requires an Atlassian Cloud site: do not offer it for Data Center.
- Jira and Confluence Data Center: the `jira-confluence-mcp` skill in `air-gapped/skills` sets up `mcp-atlassian`, including in an air gap.
- `crystaldba/postgres-mcp` is stale (last release 0.3.0, 2025-05-16): do not offer it.
- Other maintained reference servers, only when the user asks: Filesystem, Memory, Sequential Thinking, Time. The Everything server is a test server for client builders. Source: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers.

## Servers that stay off

`fetch` (`mcp-server-fetch`) and web search stay off by default: fetching is the server's job, it refuses private, loopback and link-local addresses unless `--allow-private-ips` is set, and web search leaves the network. Add `fetch` only when the user names an internal target, and then limit it with `--allowed-hosts`.

Also off: the claude.ai connectors and the official plugin marketplace of Claude Code, the `$skill-installer` of Codex CLI, and `codex mcp login` (the Egress table of each catalog entry).

## Offline install routes

None is documented in the servers' READMEs; these are the routes the research found. The skill writes them into the transfer manifest. A person runs them on the connected workstation through `airgap-transfer`.

- Python packages (`mcp-server-git`, `mcp-atlassian`): PyPI ships `py3-none-any` wheels. Download them with `pip download`, carry the folder in, then run `pip install --no-index --find-links=DIR`. Python 3.10 or newer (Fetch needs 3.11.5 or newer). Source: https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/user_guide/.
- npm packages: the reference servers need Node 24 or newer. Each tarball has runtime dependencies (zod, `@modelcontextprotocol/server` and others) that must be mirrored too: get the tarballs with `npm pack` for the package and each dependency.
- Images: build from the repository's Dockerfile, for example `cd src/git && docker build -t mcp/git .` for the git server. The Docker Hub `mcp/*` images are not used: they are stale (`latest` last updated 2025-06-16 for filesystem and git, 2025-05-02 for memory). Source: https://hub.docker.com/v2/namespaces/mcp/repositories/filesystem/tags.
- Binaries and images published by the project itself (Gitea, MCP Toolbox, `mcp-atlassian`): carry the release binary or the image, with the checksum or digest the release page gives.

## Where each tool reads MCP configuration

| Tool | MCP configuration | Central control |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen Code | `mcpServers` in user or project settings | `mcp.allowed` and `mcp.excluded` |
| Codex CLI | `[mcp_servers.<name>]` in `~/.codex/config.toml` or a trusted `.codex/config.toml` | an `mcp_servers` allowlist in `requirements.toml`; an empty one disables all MCP servers |
| opencode | `mcp.servers`; `"oauth": false` stops OAuth discovery for remote servers | policies on `mcp.use` |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude.json` (user and local scope), `.mcp.json` (project); add a server with `claude mcp add --transport stdio <name> -- <command>` | `managed-mcp.json`, `allowedMcpServers`, `deniedMcpServers` |

The shape of an entry for a stdio server differs per tool and is not in the research for Qwen Code, Codex CLI and opencode: take it from the tool's MCP page, listed in the catalog entry's Evidence.

## Skills inside the network

| Tool | Reads skills from | Central location |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen Code | `~/.qwen/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, `.qwen/skills`, `.agents/skills`; `.claude/skills` only through `skills.directories` | `skills.directories` |
| Codex CLI | `.agents/skills` from the working directory up to the repository root, `$HOME/.agents/skills` | `/etc/codex/skills` |
| opencode | `~/.config/opencode/skills`, `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, project `.opencode/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills` | the `skills` array (file paths only: URL entries are fetched) |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, project `.claude/skills/`; `.agents/skills` is not listed | `/etc/claude-code/.claude/skills/` |

So `.agents/skills` reaches Codex CLI, opencode and Qwen Code. Claude Code needs `.claude/skills`, which opencode also reads.

`air-gapped/skills` (https://github.com/air-gapped/skills, MIT, 78 installable reference skills) has per-tool skills under `.claude/skills/<name>`. Point to these; do not copy them:

| Skill | For |
|---|---|
| `vllm-tool-parsers` | choosing `--tool-call-parser` per model family, custom parsers, a debugging playbook (last verified against vLLM v0.33.0) |
| `opencode-ci-harness` | opencode v2 against OpenAI-, Responses- or Messages-compatible endpoints; diagnoses model, chat-template and tool-parser failures |
| `claude-code-ci-harness` | Claude Code headless against any Anthropic Messages-compatible endpoint |
| `messages-api`, `chat-completions-api`, `responses-api` | the three APIs as third-party protocols; `responses-api` includes Codex CLI |
| `jira-confluence-mcp` | `mcp-atlassian`, including in an air gap |
| `airgap-vetting` | listed as related; the research did not read it |

Each goes to section 6 of the transfer manifest. `airgap-transfer` treats it as a manual item: the user adds a copy of the skill's folder at a commit they choose, and nobody fetches one for them.
